entries.title: Started Harvard's CS50
entries.summary: CS50: Introduction to Computer Science, Harvard's course on problem solving and programming, from C to Python, SQL and the web.

entries.title: Reviewed pre-algebra
entries.summary: Rebuilt the math foundations: arithmetic, fractions, ratios and solving basic equations.

entries.title: Read Introduction to Financial Accounting
entries.org: Horngren, Sundem, Elliott and Philbrick, 11th edition (Pearson)
entries.summary: The core of financial accounting: the accounting cycle, the financial statements and how to read and analyse them.

entries.title: Studied Intermediate Algebra
entries.org: Richard Rusczyk and Mathew Crawford (Art of Problem Solving)
entries.summary: Algebra through problem solving: polynomials, functions, inequalities, sequences and series.

entries.title: Studied Boolean algebra
entries.org: J. Eldon Whitesitt, Boolean Algebra and Its Applications (Dover)
entries.summary: Sets, symbolic logic and Boolean algebra, applied to switching circuits: the math underneath digital logic.

entries.title: Read Code by Charles Petzold
entries.org: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software (Microsoft Press)
entries.summary: How computers work from the ground up: from codes and relays to logic gates, memory and a working processor.

entries.title: Worked through MDN's HTML docs
entries.summary: The structure of web pages: elements, semantics, forms and accessibility.

entries.title: Read “About Bootstrapping, and why it's important”
entries.summary: Why trust in software depends on the chain of compilers that built it, and how projects rebuild that chain from small, hand-checkable code.

entries.title: Started MDN's Learn web development
entries.summary: MDN's structured path through building for the web, from the first page to styling and scripting it.

entries.title: Worked through MDN's JavaScript docs
entries.summary: The language itself: values, functions, objects, the DOM and asynchronous code.

entries.title: Read Grokking Algorithms
entries.summary: Algorithms, illustrated: binary search, sorting, recursion, hash tables, graph search, Dijkstra's algorithm and dynamic programming.

entries.title: Worked through the Python docs
entries.summary: The official Python tutorial and reference: the language, its data structures and the standard library.

entries.title: Worked through MDN's CSS docs
entries.summary: Styling and layout: the cascade, the box model, flexbox and grid.

entries.title: Read The C Programming Language
entries.summary: C from the people who made it: types, control flow, pointers and arrays, structures and the standard library.

entries.title: Read How Terminals Work
entries.summary: An explainer on what a terminal actually is and how it works under the shell.

entries.title: Read Programming the World Wide Web
entries.summary: Client- and server-side web programming: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP and the pieces that connect them.
